cues.say: Component 22: Dashboards and alerts. Live charts of the system's health, plus automatic pages to the on-call person when a number crosses a line. You'll bring this up during go-live prep.
Think of it as: A car dashboard, with warning lights. Use it for launch day, and every day after.
Here's a real scenario. Game day, 3:40 PM: held orders climb, but paid goes flat.
Without it: Only errors and latency watched: both look normal.
Customers can't pay, and nobody knows.
With it: Alert: held minus paid above 50 for 3 minutes.
Runbook: check Stripe's status; if it's down, pause orders.
Why it works: The right number tells on-call what's wrong, not just that something is.
In the interview, say: If errors pass 2% for 2 minutes, I turn on the waiting room.
A few related terms you may hear.
Golden signals: Latency, traffic, errors, saturation (how full).
Business metrics: Orders a minute, held versus paid, stock left.
p ninety-five: 95% of requests are faster than this. Shows the slow tail.
Runbook: A written if this fires, do this, with an owner.
Logs, traces: Event records, and one request followed step by step.
SLO: The target, like 99.9% of checkouts under 1 second.
